Telford and Wrekin's population increased by around 18,900 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 190,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Telford and Wrekin increased by 11.3%, from just over 166,600 in 2011 to around 185,500 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Telford and Wrekin was home to around 4.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 4.1 in 2011. This area was close to the median population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Telford and Wrekin than across the West Midlands

Median age in Telford and Wrekin

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Telford and Wrekin increased by one year, from 38 to 39 years of age.

This area had a slightly lower average (median) age than the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a slightly lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 6,100 (an increase of 20.0%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 1,300 (3.4% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Telford and Wrekin residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 158,500 Telford and Wrekin residents said they were born in England. This represented 85.4% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 148,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 88.9% of Telford and Wrekin's population.

Poland was the next most represented, with just under 3,500 Telford and Wrekin residents reporting this country of birth (1.9%). This figure was up from around 2,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.3% of the population of Telford and Wrekin.

The number of Telford and Wrekin residents born in Wales remained close to 3,100 between the last two census (from 1.9% of the local population in 2011 to 1.6% in 2021)

In 2021, 85.4% of Telford and Wrekin residents reported their country of birth as England

Rise in private renting

Telford and Wrekin saw the West Midlands' largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of privately-rented homes (from 15.0% in 2011 to 21.2% in 2021).

Stoke-on-Trent (from 14.4% to 20.3%) and Wolverhampton (from 13.2% to 19.0%) saw the West Midlands' next largest increases in the percentage of privately-rented homes.

Every local authority area across the West Midlands saw a rise in the percentage of privately-rented homes, as the regional percentage grew from 14.0% to 17.9%.

Private renting in Telford and Wrekin increased by 6.2 percentage points

Unpaid care in Telford and Wrekin

In 2021, 4.8% of Telford and Wrekin residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 6.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%) than in Telford and Wrekin (2.0 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Telford and Wrekin decreased by 2.0 percentage points

National identity in Telford and Wrekin

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Telford and Wrekin (3.1 percentage points) than in nearby Shropshire (1.0 percentage points).

In Telford and Wrekin, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 4.2% in 2011 to 7.2% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Shropshire increased from 2.7% to 3.6%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Telford and Wrekin increased from 0.4% to 1.1%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 15.2% to 55.7%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Telford and Wrekin increased by 3.1 percentage points

Religion in Telford and Wrekin

In 2021, 40.9% of Telford and Wrekin residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.4% in 2011. The rise of 13.6 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Telford and Wrekin. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.6% of people in Telford and Wrekin described themselves as Christian (down from 61.7%), while 5.6% did not state their religion (down from 6.6% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

Change in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in nearby Shropshire (3.7 percentage points) than in Telford and Wrekin (1.2 percentage points).

In Telford and Wrekin, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 57.3% in 2011 to 56.1% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Shropshire decreased from 58.5% to 54.8%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Telford and Wrekin fell from 4.4% to 2.8%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 19.8% to 21.2%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Telford and Wrekin decreased by 1.2 percentage points

Working hours in Telford and Wrekin

In 2021, 8.4% of Telford and Wrekin residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (8.5%).

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.1%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 11.5% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 61.4% to 63.4%.

This area had the region’s third lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week. Across the region, only Nuneaton and Bedworth (8.1%) and Stoke-on-Trent (8.2%) had a lower percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Telford and Wrekin decreased by 0.2 percentage points

Family in Telford and Wrekin

Of Telford and Wrekin households, 18.3% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in five households (19.7%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.0% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 6.7% to 6.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Telford and Wrekin (1.3 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (1.0 percentage points, from 16.9% to 15.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Telford and Wrekin decreased by 1.3 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Telford and Wrekin residents aged 16 years and over, 36.5% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 32.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (44.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 47.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Telford and Wrekin that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 10.2% to 10.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Telford and Wrekin (3.6 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the West Midlands (3.4 percentage points, from 33.7% to 37.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Telford and Wrekin increased by 3.6 percentage points

Disability in Telford and Wrekin

In 2021, 9.1% of Telford and Wrekin residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 10.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over one in nine people (11.4%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.9% in 2011. The proportion of Telford and Wrekin residents who were not disabled increased from 78.4% to 79.5%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Telford and Wrekin (1.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Telford and Wrekin decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Health in Telford and Wrekin

In 2021, 44.2% of Telford and Wrekin residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 42.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.9% to 34.7%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Telford and Wrekin residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.5% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.6% to 5.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Telford and Wrekin increased by 1.8 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Telford and Wrekin

In 2021, 2.9% of Telford and Wrekin residents identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category, up from 1.1% in 2011. The 1.8 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" ethnic group increased from 3.3% to 4.5%, while across England the percentage increased from 3.5% to 4.2%.

In 2021, 88.2% of people in Telford and Wrekin identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 92.7% in 2011), while 5.4% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 4.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 1.8% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
